intro: A ratio is a count of parts. Every question here comes down to one move: **find what one part is worth**, then count parts. No letters are needed.

There are ten short lessons. The first six follow what the papers set; the last four are kinds found only in practice sets. Go in order the first time. If 3 : 4 and "joining two ratios" are new to you, do those two basics first.
What the papers ask (Stage A count in Quick revision: 23 IBPS Clerk papers and 12 sister papers, all memory-based):
| Adding or taking away changes the ratio (RP3) | Confirmed, 4 papers | RP3 |
| Joining ratios, with a total or an average (RP1) | Confirmed, 3 papers | RP1 |
| Income, expenditure and savings (RP4) | Confirmed, 3 papers | RP4 |
| Dividing an amount (RP2) | Confirmed, 2 papers | RP2 |
| Groups inside a group (RP5) | Confirmed, 2 papers | RP5 |
| Percent change on each term, coins, proportion, harder forms | Bank only | RP6 to RP10 |
after: That is the whole topic. The **Quick revision** tab has the conversion grid, the drills and the practice ladder.
Ratio is also the engine inside Ages, Partnership, Mixtures and Time & Work; those topics build on these lessons.

lessons.title: A ratio is a count of parts
lessons.plain: The starting point: turning words, fractions and percents into parts, and comparing ratios.
teach: A ratio such as 3 : 5 says: cut both things into equal parts; the first has 3, the second has 5. The parts are what you count; rupees come later.
Most questions start by turning something else into parts:
| The question says | In parts |
| A is 25% more than B | A : B = 125 : 100 = 5 : 4 |
| A is 20% less than B | A : B = 80 : 100 = 4 : 5 |
To **compare** ratios, turn each into a decimal (7 : 9 is 0.78) or cross-multiply two at a time.
An expression such as (4x + 3y) : (4x - 3y) with x : y = 5 : 3 needs no algebra: put 5 and 3 straight in.

steps: Equal products mean A, B and C are like 1/3, 1/5 and 1/6.
Multiply by 30, the LCM of 3, 5 and 6: 10, 6 and 5.

check.q: A is 40% more than B. What is A : B?
check.why: A = 140 when B = 100, so 140 : 100 = 7 : 5. (5 : 7 is the right numbers in the wrong order.)

tags: An expression: put the numbers in.

lessons.title: Joining ratios, with a total or an average
lessons.plain: New: two ratios share a person, and the question gives a total or an average.
teach: When two ratios share a person, **make that person's number the same in both**, then write one ratio for all three.
A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 6 : 5. B is 4 and 6; make both 12: A : B = 9 : 12 and B : C = 12 : 10. So A : B : C = 9 : 12 : 10.
Then use the number the question gives. An **average** is a total in disguise: average x how many = total. Total / total parts = one part.
Sometimes there is no ratio at first, only links such as "A is 8 more than C". Find the numbers from the links, then write their ratio.
Checked papers: this was asked in three IBPS Clerk papers (2017, Dec 2021, Oct 2025).

example.q: A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 6 : 5. A + B + C = 155. Find C.
steps: Make B equal: 9 : 12 and 12 : 10, so A : B : C = 9 : 12 : 10.

check.q: A : B = 2 : 5 and B : C = 3 : 4. What is A : B : C?
check.why: Make B equal to 15: A : B = 6 : 15 and B : C = 15 : 20. (2 : 5 : 4 just writes the numbers side by side without making B equal.)

lessons.title: Dividing an amount
lessons.plain: New: an amount is shared, and you are told the ratio, a difference, or how the shares relate.
teach: **Total / total parts = one part.** Rs 1,560 in 5 : 8 is 13 parts, so one part is 120.
If a **difference** is given instead ("C gets Rs 1,200 more than A" with 3 : 5 : 7), the difference is 7 - 3 = 4 parts.
If shares are described by **fractions of each other** ("A gets 2/3 of B, B gets 1/4 of C"), pick a handy number for the last person: C = 12 makes B = 3 and A = 2.
If shares are described by **differences** ("A gets 4,000 more than B, C gets 8,000 more than B"), take the extras off the total and split the rest equally.
Checked papers: IBPS Clerk 2018 and IBPS PO 2025 each set one.

example.q: Rs 9,000 is divided among A, B and C so that A gets Rs 1,000 more than B and C gets Rs 2,000 more than B. Find C's share.
steps: That is three equal shares: B = 2,000.

check.q: Rs 2,400 is divided between P and Q in the ratio 3 : 5. How much more does Q get than P?
check.why: 8 parts = 2,400, one part = 300. The gap is 2 parts = 600. (300 is one part; 1,500 is Q's whole share.)

tags: A difference of shares is given.
Shares as fractions of each other.

lessons.title: When numbers are added or taken away
lessons.plain: New: the two amounts change and the ratio changes with them. This is the kind the papers set most.
teach: Ask one question first: **what did not change?** It decides how you match the two ratios.
| What happens | What stays the same | Make this equal in both ratios |
| the same number is added to (or taken from) each | the difference | the difference of the terms |
| one gives some to the other | the total | the sum of the terms |
| only one of them changes | the other one | the other one's parts |
Then the term that changed moved by some number of parts, and that is the rupees (or people) the question names. One part found, everything follows.
Checked papers: four papers (IBPS Clerk Oct 2025 and 2025, SBI Clerk Sep 2025 twice).

example.q: Two numbers are in the ratio 4 : 7. If 9 is added to each, the ratio becomes 5 : 8. Find the numbers.
steps: Added to each, so the difference stays: 7 - 4 = 3 and 8 - 5 = 3, already equal.
The first went from 4 parts to 5 parts by adding 9: one part = 9.

check.q: A and B have money in the ratio 3 : 2. A gives Rs 100 to B and the ratio becomes 1 : 1. How much did A have at first?
check.why: The total stays at 5 parts, so 1 : 1 is 2.5 : 2.5. A lost half a part = 100, so one part = 200 and A had 600. (300 treats the 100 as one whole part.)

tags: The same number added to each.
Money moves across: the total stays.

shortcut.title: Cross-multiplying when nothing lines up
text: If the totals or differences do not match neatly, cross-multiply once. 3 : 2 becomes 19 : 26 after 16 moves from A to B. With A = 3k and B = 2k: (3k - 16) x 26 = (2k + 16) x 19.
Use it only when matching the parts feels slow; it is one line of algebra.

lessons.title: Income, expenditure and savings
lessons.plain: New: three linked amounts. Income is always expenditure plus savings.
teach: **Income = expenditure + savings**, in rupees and in parts. Income : savings = 16 : 3 means expenditure is 13 parts.

**Two people save the same amount.** Their income parts minus expenditure parts must stand for the same rupees. Scale the ratios until the leftovers match: incomes 5 : 4 with expenditures 7 : 5? Write incomes as 10 : 8; then both leave 3.
**Spends a fraction.** "Spends 3/11" saves 8/11. "Spends 25%, then 20% of the rest, then 15% of the rest" leaves 0.75 x 0.8 x 0.85 = 0.51 of the income.
**Something rises by a percent.** Work it part by part: new income - new expenditure = new savings.
Checked papers: IBPS Clerk 2021 and 2024, IBPS RRB Clerk Dec 2025.

example.q: The incomes of A and B are in the ratio 3 : 2 and their expenditures 5 : 3. Each saves Rs 2,000. Find A's income.
steps: Write incomes as 6 : 4 so that, with expenditures 5 : 3, both leave 1 unit.

check.q: A man's income and expenditure are in the ratio 7 : 5. He saves Rs 4,000. What is his income?
check.why: Savings = 7 - 5 = 2 parts = 4,000, so one part = 2,000 and income = 14,000. (10,000 is the expenditure.)

tags: Percent rises: how much more is saved?
Income to savings, then both change.

lessons.title: Groups inside a group
lessons.plain: New: a whole is split one way (boys and girls) and each part is split again.
teach: Work **outside in**: split the whole first, then split each piece by its own ratio or percent.
Take 100 people when only percents are given: 68% literate means 68 and 32.
**A shared count** is a gift. "Both sections have the same number of girls": the difference of the section totals is then exactly the difference of the boys.
**A percent of each group** (20% of boys, 25% of girls): weight by the parts. With boys : girls = 3 : 2, (3 x 20 + 2 x 25) / 5 = 22%. The plain average, 22.5%, is the usual wrong option.
Checked papers: IBPS Clerk 2018 and 2024.

example.q: A college has 1,200 students, boys and girls in the ratio 7 : 5. 3/7 of the boys and 2/5 of the girls live in the hostel. How many live in the hostel?

check.q: Boys and girls are in the ratio 3 : 2. 10% of the boys and 20% of the girls play chess. What percent of the class plays chess?
check.why: (3 x 10 + 2 x 20) / 5 = 14%. (15% is the plain average, which ignores that there are more boys.)

more.q: Sections A and B have 150 and 190 students. Both have the same number of girls, and the boys are in the ratio 2 : 3. How many girls are in each section?
more.why: The 40 extra students in B are all boys, and boys differ by 1 part: one part = 40, boys 80 and 120, girls 150 - 80 = 70.

more.q: 60% of a village is literate. Literate men and women are 2 : 1; illiterate men and women are 1 : 3. What is the ratio of literate women to illiterate women?
more.why: Take 100: literate women 60 x 1/3 = 20, illiterate women 40 x 3/4 = 30. 20 : 30 = 2 : 3.

lessons.title: A different percent change on each term
lessons.plain: New: each term of the ratio grows or shrinks by its own percent.
teach: **Multiply each term by its own factor**, then tidy up. Salaries 3 : 4 with rises of 20% and 10%: 3 x 1.2 : 4 x 1.1 = 3.6 : 4.4 = 9 : 11.
Percents are never added to or subtracted from a ratio. 4 : 5 with rises of 25% and 20% is 5 : 6, not anything with 45 in it.
If the starting point is a percent comparison ("males are 60% more than females"), turn it into a ratio first: 160 : 100.
If a difference or total is given after the change, work in parts: 3 parts becomes 3.6 parts, 2 parts becomes 2.8 parts, and the gap of 0.8 parts is the number given.
No paper in the sample set this; it is common in practice sets.

example.q: The prices of two items are in the ratio 5 : 6. The first rises by 20% and the second by 25%. What is the new ratio?

check.q: Salaries of P and Q are in the ratio 4 : 5. P gets a 25% rise and Q a 20% rise. What is the new ratio?
check.why: 4 x 1.25 = 5 and 5 x 1.2 = 6. (4 : 5 assumes the rises cancel; they do not.)

tags: Start from a percent comparison; one rises, one falls.

lessons.title: Coins, and shares per head
lessons.plain: New: the ratio counts coins or people, but the total is in rupees.
teach: **Coins.** The ratio is of the number of coins, not their value. Make one **set**: for Rs 1, Rs 2 and Rs 5 coins in 5 : 3 : 2, one set is five Rs 1, three Rs 2 and two Rs 5 = 5 + 6 + 10 = Rs 21. Total / value of one set = number of sets.
Paise coins: work in paise, or write 50p as 0.5 and 25p as 0.25.
Read carefully whether the ratio is of numbers or of values. If it is of values, divide each by the face value to get the numbers.
**Shares per head.** "Each man, woman and child gets in the ratio 4 : 3 : 2" with 5 men, 8 women and 12 children: the groups' shares are 5 x 4 : 8 x 3 : 12 x 2 = 20 : 24 : 24.
No paper in the sample set this; it is common in practice sets.

example.q: A bag has 50 paise, Rs 1 and Rs 2 coins in the ratio 4 : 3 : 2, worth Rs 90 in all. How many Rs 1 coins are there?
steps: One set: four 50p, three Rs 1 and two Rs 2 = 2 + 3 + 4 = Rs 9.

check.q: A box has Rs 1, Rs 2 and Rs 5 coins in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1, worth Rs 120. How many Rs 2 coins are there?
check.why: One set is worth 3 + 4 + 5 = Rs 12, so there are 10 sets and 20 Rs 2 coins. (40 takes the Rs 2 coins' value instead of their number.)

tags: Three kinds, four of the smallest.

lessons.title: Proportion
lessons.plain: New: two ratios that are equal, and the special words third, fourth and mean proportional.
teach: a : b = c : d is a **proportion**. The rule that does all the work: **a x d = b x c** (outer pair = inner pair).
| Word | Meaning | Formula |
| fourth proportional to a, b, c | a : b = c : x | b x c / a |
| third proportional to a, b | a : b = b : x | b x b / a |
| mean proportional of a, b | a : x = x : b | square root of a x b |
"What must be subtracted from each of four numbers so that they are in proportion?" Try the options: subtract, then test first x fourth = second x third.
No paper in the sample set this. It is quick, so learn it after the others.

example.q: Find the mean proportional between 9 and 16.

check.q: What is the fourth proportional to 4, 10 and 6?
check.why: 4 : 10 = 6 : x, so x = 10 x 6 / 4 = 15. (24 multiplies 4 x 6 and stops.)

tags: Subtract to make a proportion: test the options.

more.q: What is the third proportional to 9 and 12?

lessons.title: Harder forms
lessons.plain: New: five less common forms. Each is one extra step on what you know.
teach: **A mistaken division.** Work out both divisions and subtract. Intended 2 : 3 : 4 but done as 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4 (= 6 : 4 : 3).
**Shares reduced by fixed amounts** before the ratio holds: take the reductions off the total first, split the rest, then add each reduction back.
**A fraction of one equals a fraction of the other** (4/15 of A = 2/5 of B): A : B = 2/5 : 4/15 = 3 : 2. The fractions swap sides.
**Squares.** Numbers in 3 : 4 : 5 with squares adding to 1,250: 9 + 16 + 25 = 50 squared parts, so one squared part = 25 and one part = 5.
**LCM.** Two numbers in 3 : 5 (no common factor) have LCM = 3 x 5 x one part.
**Sums of pairs** (a + b) : (b + c) : (c + a): the three add up to twice a + b + c.

example.q: Rs 1,000 was to be divided between A and B in the ratio 1 : 4, but by mistake it was divided 4 : 1. How much more did A get?

check.q: Two numbers are in the ratio 2 : 3 and their LCM is 48. What is their sum?
check.why: LCM = 2 x 3 x one part = 6 parts = 48, so one part = 8. Numbers 16 and 24, sum 40. (48 is the LCM itself.)

tags: A fraction of one equals a fraction of the other.
